Testicular Cancer: The patient's presentation of painless scrotal swelling, bilateral testicular enlargement without tenderness, and scrotal ultrasound showing large, solid masses in both testes are consistent with testicular cancer. The histologic examination demonstrating a pleomorphic tumor composed of three distinct cell types also supports this diagnosis. Although serum tumor markers such as alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG), and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) are within normal limits, this does not rule out testicular cancer, as these markers are elevated in only a subset of patients with this disease.
Lymphoma: While lymphoma is a possible diagnosis, the absence of lymphadenopathy or extranodal lymphomatous masses on positron emission tomography–computed tomography scan and the lack of elevated serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) levels make this diagnosis less likely. Additionally, the histologic examination did not demonstrate lymphoid malignancy, further decreasing the likelihood of lymphoma. However, lymphoma cannot be completely ruled out without further evaluation and testing.
